text: Molecules with polar surface area above the training median (17.1 A^2) have more favourable hydration free energy.
Molecules with at least one hydrogen-bond donor have more favourable hydration free energy.
Molecules containing a hydroxyl group have more favourable (more negative) hydration free energy.
Molecules with two or more hydrogen-bond acceptors have more favourable hydration free energy.
Molecules containing a primary amine not attached to a carbonyl have more favorable hydration free energy than molecules without a primary amine at matched TPSA.
Molecules with MolLogP above 3 have less favorable hydration free energy than molecules below this threshold, independently of polar surface area.
Molecules with more than one rotatable bond have less favorable hydration free energy than more rigid molecules of the same polar surface area.
Molecules containing an aromatic N-H group have more favorable hydration free energy than molecules without one, even at matched TPSA.
Molecules with FractionCSP3 above 0.8 are less favorably hydrated than less-saturated molecules of the same TPSA.
Molecules containing an N-halogen bond have less favorable hydration free energy than N-alkyl counterparts of identical polar surface area.
Molecules containing a thioketone or thione C=S group have less favorable hydration free energy than corresponding oxo-carbonyl compounds at matched TPSA.
Molecules containing a nitrile group have less favorable hydration free energy than other molecules of comparable TPSA.
